prompt: In one of the following pictures exactly three quarters of all objects are hearts. Which one is it?

solutions.title: Use the middle number
solutions.body:
The five numbers are evenly spaced around 2003, so their sum is $5 \times 2003 = 10015$.

**Answer: (E) 10015**

prompt: At the picture below you can see a road from town A to town B (a solid line), and a detour of a renovated interval A'B', marked as a dashed line. How many km further does one have to travel using the detour?

solutions.title: Compare the two routes
solutions.body:
The detour goes 3 km down, then along a stretch exactly as long as A'B', then 3 km back up. The middle part is the same length as the road it replaces, so the extra distance is $3 + 3 = 6$ km.

**Answer: (C) 6 km**

solutions.title: The length of A'B' doesn't matter
solutions.body:
Call the length of A'B' $x$ km. The normal road there is $x$ km; the detour is $3 + x + 3 = x + 6$ km. Whatever $x$ is, the detour is 6 km longer.

**Answer: (C) 6 km**

prompt: Jerome was 4 years old when his sister was born. Today he celebrates his 9th birthday. What is the age difference between him and his sister?

solutions.title: The difference never changes
solutions.body:
When his sister was born, Jerome was 4 years older than her. Both get one year older every year, so the difference always stays 4 years.

**Answer: (A) 4 years**

solutions.title: Work out the sister's age
solutions.body:
Jerome is 9 now, and his sister was born 4 years after him, so she is $9 - 4 = 5$. Difference: $9 - 5 = 4$ years.

**Answer: (A) 4 years**

prompt: In the picture the distance $AC = 10$ m, $BD = 15$ m, $AD = 22$ m. Find the distance $BC$.
Hedgehog Mark complained to his friends: "*If I had picked up twice as many apples as I really did, I would have 24 apples more than I have now.*" How many apples did Mark pick up?
Gabriella brings to Joseph a basket with apples and oranges. Joseph has eaten a half of all apples and one third of all oranges. Which part of the fruits remained in the basket?

choices.text: more than half of all fruits
less than half of all fruits
less than a third of all fruits

solutions.title: Compare with eating half of everything
solutions.body:
If Joseph had eaten half of the apples and half of the oranges, exactly half of all the fruits would remain. But he ate only one third of the oranges, which is less than half, so more oranges remain than in that case. So more than half of all fruits remain.

**Answer: (B) more than half of all fruits**

solutions.title: Try numbers
solutions.body:
Say there are 6 apples and 6 oranges (12 fruits). He eats 3 apples and 2 oranges, so $12 - 5 = 7$ fruits remain — more than half of 12. Any numbers give the same result, because half of the apples stay and more than half of the oranges stay.

**Answer: (B) more than half of all fruits**

prompt: How many yellow squares must you paint red so that the number of red squares is exactly half of the number of yellow squares?

solutions.title: Red must be one third of all squares
solutions.body:
The grid has $6 \times 4 = 24$ squares, 5 of them red. If red is half of yellow, then for every 1 red there are 2 yellow, so red is one third of all squares: $24 \div 3 = 8$. We need $8 - 5 = 3$ more red squares.

**Answer: (B) 3**

solutions.title: Check the choices
solutions.body:
Paint 3 squares red: 8 red and 16 yellow, and 8 is half of 16 ✓. Painting 2 would give 7 red and 17 yellow; painting 4 would give 9 red and 15 yellow — neither works.

**Answer: (B) 3**

prompt: Chris constructed the brick in the picture using red and blue cubes of the same size. The outside of the brick is completely red, but all cubes used inside are blue. How many blue cubes did Chris use?

Betty likes calculating the sum of the digits that she sees on her digital clock (for instance, if the clock shows 21:17, then Betty gets 11). What is the biggest sum she can get if the clock is a 24-hour clock?

The picture below shows 9 pencils and a weight of 30 g on a balance scale. The picture on the right shows one of the same pencils, a pen, and a weight of 15 g. Both scales are balanced. How many grams does the pen weigh?

solutions.title: Remove pencils from both sides
solutions.body:
On the first scale there are 7 pencils on the left and 2 pencils plus 30 g on the right. Taking 2 pencils from each side keeps it balanced: 5 pencils = 30 g, so one pencil weighs 6 g. On the second scale, pencil + pen = 15 g, so the pen weighs $15 - 6 = 9$ g.

**Answer: (D) 9 g**

solutions.title: Check the choices
solutions.body:
If a pencil weighs 6 g: left side $7 \times 6 = 42$ g, right side $2 \times 6 + 30 = 42$ g ✓. Then pen $= 15 - 6 = 9$ g.

**Answer: (D) 9 g**

prompt: In a class there are 29 children. 12 children have a sister and 18 children have a brother. Tina, Bert, and Anne have no brother and no sister. How many children in that class have both a brother and a sister?

There are five houses on Colour Street: a blue, a red, a yellow, a pink, and a green one. The houses stand in a row and are numbered from 1 to 5.

Determine the color of house #3 using the following clues:
- The numbers of the blue and yellow houses are even.
- The red house is next to the blue house only.
- The blue house is between the green and red houses.

solutions.title: Place blue, then red, then green
solutions.body:
The even numbers are 2 and 4, so blue is #2 or #4 and yellow is the other one. The red house has only one neighbour (the blue one), so it is at an end: #1 next to blue #2, or #5 next to blue #4. Green is on the other side of blue: if blue is #2, green is #3; if blue is #4, green is #3. Either way house #3 is green.

**Answer: (E) Green**

solutions.title: Rule out colours for #3
solutions.body:
#3 is odd, so it is not blue or yellow. Red is at an end (it has only one neighbour), so it is not #3. Blue (at #2 or #4) has red on one side and green on the other; the other side of blue from the end is #3. So #3 is green, and pink is the remaining end house.

**Answer: (E) Green**

prompt: Four numbers are placed in the small squares in the table below. If the sum of the numbers of the first row is 3, the sum of the numbers of the second row is 8 and the sum of the numbers of the first column is 4, what is the sum of the numbers in the second column?

solutions.title: Total of the table
solutions.body:
Adding the two rows gives the sum of all four numbers: $3 + 8 = 11$. The first column has 4 of that, so the second column has $11 - 4 = 7$.

**Answer: (C) 7**

solutions.title: Try an example
solutions.body:
For instance, first row 1 and 2 (sum 3), second row 3 and 5 (sum 8). The first column is $1 + 3 = 4$ ✓, and the second column is $2 + 5 = 7$.

**Answer: (C) 7**

prompt: The first three figures of a pattern are constructed from triangles, as shown. There is one triangle on the first figure, 4 triangles on the second figure, and 9 triangles on the third figure. If the pattern is extended with several more figures, how many triangles will be there on the fifth figure?

solutions.title: Add odd numbers
solutions.body:
Each new figure adds a new row along the bottom: 1, then $1 + 3 = 4$, then $1 + 3 + 5 = 9$. The fourth figure has $9 + 7 = 16$ and the fifth $16 + 9 = 25$.

**Answer: (C) 25**

solutions.title: Square numbers
solutions.body:
1, 4, 9 are $1 \times 1$, $2 \times 2$, $3 \times 3$. The fifth figure has $5 \times 5 = 25$ triangles.

**Answer: (C) 25**
